base_member_text: READ_LOGICAL: type mismatch only warns (L178-L180, no STOP) unlike INTEGER/FLOAT/STRING which MPI_FINALIZE+STOP; value is then set from first character only (L182-L183), so CHECK_CONSISTENCY_TYPE's 'logical' result is not actually required
audit_member_text: Logical recognition accepts only a one-character uppercase T or F at L278-L282, and READ_LOGICAL sets true only when the first character is uppercase T at L182-L183. Lowercase t/f and standard .TRUE./.FALSE. forms are diagnosed as non-logical and then silently mapped false rather than rejected or parsed.

base_member_text: READ_VALUE: successful match RETURNs @L253 without CLOSE(10); CLOSE @L260 is reached only via the EOF path (label 100 @L258) — unit 10 apparently left open on every successful key lookup (relation L237/L253/L260); also each READ_* call re-OPENs unit 10 per key
audit_member_text: READ_VALUE returns immediately on a match at L251-L253 without CLOSE(10); CLOSE occurs only on EOF at L258-L260. Successful reads leave unit 10 connected. Reopening/rewinding the same unit repeatedly may work for the same file, but switching InputFileName while connected is nonportable and the successful path never releases the unit.

base_member_text: License header FILE line @L14 says 'main.F' but this file is the INPUT_READ module (mod_input) — header/file-name mismatch
ERR_IF_ONE has INTENT(OUT) in READ_STRING @L193 and READ_VALUE @L230 but no INTENT attribute in READ_INTEGER @L90, READ_FLOAT @L127, READ_LOGICAL @L162

CHECK_CONSISTENCY_TYPE returns VTYPE 'INTEGER' in uppercase @L298 while other types are lowercase ('float' @L296, 'logical' @L280, 'string' @L288); the comparisons @L107 ('INTEGER'), @L143 ('float'), @L178 ('logical'), @L211 ('string') match these exact cases — case consistency is load-bearing across subroutines
ERR_IF_ONE is initialized to 0 @L236 only inside READ_VALUE; typed readers test ERR_IF_ONE == 1 (L100, L137, L172, L204) relying on READ_VALUE having set it

audit_member_text: All four destination arguments are INTENT(OUT) (INTEGER_VAL L87, FLOAT_VAL L123, LOGICAL_VAL L158, STRING_VAL L190), but a missing key returns without assigning them at L100-L103, L137-L140, L172-L175 and L204-L207. Fortran makes an INTENT(OUT) actual argument undefined on entry, so callers cannot safely retain module initializers. This turns unchecked missing keys in io.f90—including WAVE_DATA_TYPE, ETA_LIMITER, NumberStations and the block of output flags—into undefined values rather than defaults.

CHECK_CONSISTENCY_TYPE calls a numeric string 'float' only if it contains a dot (L293-L299). Valid real inputs such as 1 or 1E-3 are classified INTEGER and rejected by READ_FLOAT at L142-L146, despite list-directed READ at L149 being able to convert them. Conversely malformed dot-containing numeric strings reach an unchecked internal READ failure.

READ_VALUE computes FRONT=index(TEXT,'=') at L249 and immediately forms TEXT(1:FRONT-1) at L250 without a FRONT==0 branch. Blank/comment-only or arbitrary non-assignment lines therefore rely on compiler handling of a substring ending at -1 and can raise a bounds error under checking builds.
